name: buick_231_oddfire
label: Buick 231 V6, odd-fire (1975-77)
based_on: Buick 231 cu in V6, odd-fire, 1975 to early 1977

sources.what: 1975 Buick Chassis Service Manual, section 6A (engine), hosted by TeamBuick. Factory document: bore/stroke, CR, numbering, firing order, valve head diameters, rocker ratio.
jeepster-commando.com 'Understanding the odd-fire V6'. Enthusiast article with a step-by-step crank-angle table for the 225/231 odd-fire; source of the interval sequence and pin positions.
Ate Up With Motor history of the Buick V6, with a bibliography. 150/90 intervals, 8.0:1, 110 hp / 175 lb-ft, even-fire arriving during 1977.
Casting-number compilation: 1975-76 231 listed as odd-fire, straight rod pin crank; 1977 listed in both odd-fire and even-fire rows.

notes: Sourced: 90 degree bank angle, bore, stroke, compression ratio, firing order 1-6-5-4-3-2 with cylinders 1-3-5 on the left bank, three shared crank pins 120 degrees apart, firing intervals 150-90-150-90-150-90, one intake and one exhaust valve per cylinder with their diameters, two-barrel carburettor on a plenum manifold, one log manifold per bank joined into a single exhaust, published peak power and torque (SAE net, 1975). The speeds of the published peaks were not found, so `engsim validate` has nothing to run at; compare against the peaks of a dyno sweep. Estimated, not sourced: rod length, valve lifts, all cam timing, carburettor throttle area, intake runner length, exhaust manifold branch length and diameter, exhaust pipe and tail pipe diameters, redline, idle, friction_scale and heat_q (tuned; both sit at the weak end of their ranges, for a 1975 emissions-era engine). Everything else is left to the derived defaults (runner diameter, plenum, pipe lengths, muffler, flywheel).

vehicle.name: Buick Skyhawk hatchback coupe (1975)
vehicle.notes: The Skyhawk's only engine was the 231 V6. A four-speed manual was standard and the Turbo Hydra-matic 350 automatic optional; no production split was found, and the automatic is modelled on my assumption that it was the commoner choice in a 1975 Buick (the four-speed's ratios were not found either). Automatic modelled as fixed ratios with a clutch; torque-converter multiplication is not modelled. Axle 2.56 is Buick's standard for the Skyhawk 231 with either gearbox. Curb weight is Wikipedia's rounded 2,800 lb for the 1975-80 Skyhawk, not a 1975 factory figure. wheel_radius_m and top speed omitted (not found).
